newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DAMRON LEADS RAIN-PLAGUED ST JUDE CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DAMRON LEADS RAIN-PLAGUED ST JUDE CLASSIC.

text.p: PGA Tour rookie Robert Damron's name remained atop the leaderboard at the rain-plagued St Jude Classic Saturday, but he got in only three third round holes before play was halted for the day.

Damron was at 13-under for the tournament and held a two-shot lead when lightning and rain suspended play. Gene Sauers, who held the lead at 10-under when play was suspended Friday, was two strokes behind Damron at 11-under, also through three holes.
Mike Hulbert and Greg Norman stood at 9-under, while 10 golfers, including Nick Price and Curtis Strange, were one stroke further back.

None of the 75 players left in the field managed to complete the third round after 106 golfers were forced to finish their second rounds Saturday morning. Thirty-six players, including Damron, had to play a full 18 holes before beginning third-round play Saturday.

Efforts to get back on track Saturday morning were further hampered when rain delayed a planned early start by some 30 minutes. Organisers said third-round play will resume at 8:30 a.m. (1230 gmt) Sunday, weather permitting.

The 24-year-old Damron joined this year's PGA Tour after finishing 16th at the 1996 Qualifying Tournament. He has compiled three top-10 finishes in 19 events this season, including a tie for third at last week's Buick Classic, which was also affected by rain.
"It's happened to me a thousand times, it will happen again," Damron said of the rain delays. "You just take it in stride and be patient."

Norman, seeking his first PGA victory of the year, completed a second-round 65. He later lipped out a birdie attempt on his first hole of the third round and remained at nine-under through three holes.

Price, competing for the first time since the June 16 death of long-time caddie and friend Jeff "Squeeky" Medlen, completed his final two second-round holes and finished with a 68. He failed to pick up any further ground in his first three holes of the third round.
Damron, who was in a group with Norman, admitted to being a bit nervous playing in such illustrious company.
"I calmed down pretty well," he said.
"I hit some solid shots and you know, the pressure of playing with the lead is fae more than playing with Norman."
